newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING lifts managed assets 17 pct in H1.
newsitem.headline: ING lifts managed assets 17 pct in H1.

text.p: Financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Tuesday that assets managed by ING Investment Management worldwide grew more than 17 percent to 185.8 billion guilders in the first six months of 1997.
"All activities - asset management for institutional clients, for investment funds and for insurance companies of ING Group - contributed to this growth," the Dutch group said.

ING said assets managed for ING insurance companies grew 18.7 percent to 121.8 billion guilders, assets managed for institutions rose 15 percent to 38.3 billion and assets managed for investment funds jumped 15.3 percent to 25.7 billion.
ING said one billion of the five billion guilder increase in institutional clients' assets under management was new money with the balance of the rise attributed to higher prices.
It said equity investments increased to 27 percent of combined assets under management for institutions, from 21 percent, mainly due to the increase in equity prices.
"All equity investments showed very high returns, exceeding the relevant benchmarks in most cases," the group said.
An ING spokeswoman said 600 million guilders of the 3.4 billion guilder increase in assets managed for investments funds was new money, all in the Netherlands.
But she said no information was available on how much of the increase in assets managed for insurance companies was due to inflows of new money and how much to higher values for existing assets.
But ING said in a statement: "The good performance and the addition of new premiums contributed to the growth of the assets under management for the insurance companies of ING Group."
